name: Linda Williams
chief_complaint: Severe chest pain radiating to left arm for 2 hours
opening_statement: I've had terrible crushing chest pain for the last 2 hours that won't go away. It's spreading down my left arm and I feel really sweaty and nauseous.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and distressed. Patient is visibly uncomfortable, clutching her chest, and concerned this might be 'the big one' like her father had.

symptoms.name: Chest pain
symptoms.onset: 2 hours ago, sudden onset at rest
symptoms.relieving_factors: Not relieved by rest or GTN spray (2 puffs taken)

rag_citations.quote: Typical cardiac chest pain is retrosternal, crushing or pressure-like, may radiate to left arm, neck or jaw, associated with diaphoresis and dyspnoea
Autonomic symptoms including diaphoresis, nausea and vomiting are common in acute MI, particularly inferior wall infarction
Gastrointestinal symptoms occur in 30-40% of acute MI cases, may be mistaken for gastritis in atypical presentations

symptoms.name: Dyspnoea
symptoms.character: Mild shortness of breath at rest

rag_citations.quote: Acute pulmonary oedema may complicate anterior wall MI due to significant LV dysfunction

past_medical_history.current_status: Suboptimally controlled, HbA1c 8.2% (last check 3 months ago)
past_medical_history.notes: Followed by GP, no endocrinologist involvement

past_medical_history.current_status: Controlled on dual therapy, usual BP 135/85 mmHg
past_medical_history.notes: Recently switched from amlodipine to perindopril due to ankle oedema

past_medical_history.current_status: On statin therapy, last LDL 2.8 mmol/L (target <2.0 for high CV risk)
BMI 32 kg/m², weight 88 kg, height 165 cm
past_medical_history.complications: Obstructive sleep apnoea (mild, not on CPAP)
past_medical_history.notes: Multiple failed weight loss attempts, referred to dietitian but did not attend

medications.name: Aspirin
medications.indication: Primary prevention in high CV risk patient

medications.name: GTN spray
medications.indication: Angina prophylaxis (prescribed 1 year ago after atypical chest pain episode)

allergies: No known drug allergies. Denies food or environmental allergies.
family_history: Father died at age 62 from myocardial infarction ('massive heart attack'). Mother alive, aged 82, has hypertension and Type 2 diabetes. One brother aged 55, healthy. No family history of sudden cardiac death or inherited cardiac conditions.

social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker, quit 10 years ago (20 pack-year history)
social_history.alcohol: Social drinker, 1-2 standard drinks per week
social_history.exercise: Minimal - walks dog 15 minutes daily, no structured exercise
social_history.living_situation: Lives with husband and two teenage children
social_history.support_network: Strong - husband is supportive, extended family nearby
social_history.mental_health: No history of anxiety or depression

cardiovascular.inspection: JVP not elevated, no visible pulsations
cardiovascular.palpation: Apex beat not displaced, no heaves or thrills
cardiovascular.auscultation: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, S4 gallop present
cardiovascular.peripheral_pulses: All pulses present and equal, no radio-radial delay

examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, bowel sounds normal
examination_findings.neurological: Alert and oriented, GCS 15, no focal deficits
examination_findings.peripheral: Mild peripheral oedema (1+), capillary refill <2 seconds

ecg.description: Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm. ST elevation 3-4 mm in leads V1-V4, I, aVL. Reciprocal ST depression in leads III, aVF. Hyperacute T waves in anterior leads.

troponin_hs.interpretation: Significantly elevated, consistent with acute MI

chest_xray.description: Mild cardiomegaly. Early pulmonary vascular congestion. No consolidation or effusion.

expected_diagnosis: STEMI (anterior wall) - LAD territory infarction complicated by early LV dysfunction

expected_management.action: Activate STEMI pathway - call cardiology/cathlab immediately
expected_management.rationale: Door-to-balloon time <90 minutes critical for myocardial salvage

expected_management.action: Aspirin 300 mg PO (chewed) + Ticagrelor 180 mg PO loading dose
expected_management.rationale: Dual antiplatelet therapy reduces mortality and stent thrombosis
expected_management.mbs_reference: PBS unrestricted for acute coronary syndrome

expected_management.action: High-flow oxygen (if SpO2 <90%), otherwise room air
expected_management.rationale: Maintain SpO2 ≥94%, avoid hyperoxia (increases infarct size)

expected_management.action: IV morphine 2.5-5 mg for pain relief
expected_management.rationale: Analgesic + reduces preload, improves patient comfort

expected_management.action: GTN sublingual/IV if ongoing pain and SBP >100 mmHg
expected_management.rationale: Reduces preload and myocardial oxygen demand

expected_management.action: Heparin 5000 units IV bolus (or enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC if transfer delay)
Primary PCI - emergency coronary angiography and stent to culprit LAD lesion
expected_management.rationale: Gold standard reperfusion therapy for STEMI, superior to thrombolysis

expected_management.action: If PCI unavailable within 90 min: Thrombolysis (tenecteplase 40 mg IV bolus)
expected_management.rationale: Time-dependent benefit in first 12 hours, reduces mortality
expected_management.mbs_reference: PBS restricted - STEMI when PCI unavailable

expected_management.action: Commence ACE inhibitor (ramipril 2.5 mg daily, titrate up) within 24 hours
expected_management.rationale: Reduces mortality and LV remodelling post-anterior MI
Early intensive lipid-lowering reduces recurrent events
expected_management.mbs_reference: PBS unrestricted for acute coronary syndrome

expected_management.action: Beta-blocker (metoprolol 25 mg BD, titrate to HR 50-60) if no contraindications
expected_management.rationale: Reduces mortality, limits infarct expansion, prevents arrhythmias

expected_management.action: Continue dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 100 mg + ticagrelor 90 mg BD) for 12 months
expected_management.rationale: Prevents stent thrombosis and recurrent ischaemic events
expected_management.mbs_reference: PBS restricted - requires Authority for ticagrelor >4 weeks

expected_management.action: Continuous cardiac monitoring for arrhythmias (VT/VF risk highest in first 48h)
expected_management.rationale: Anterior MI has high risk of heart block and ventricular arrhythmias

expected_management.action: Frusemide 20-40 mg IV if pulmonary oedema worsens (monitor electrolytes)
expected_management.rationale: Reduce pulmonary congestion from LV dysfunction
expected_management.mbs_reference: PBS unrestricted for acute heart failure

expected_management.action: Intensive diabetes management - insulin sliding scale acutely, liaise with endocrinology
expected_management.rationale: Hyperglycaemia worsens outcomes post-MI, target glucose 6-10 mmol/L

expected_management.action: Cardiac rehabilitation referral + dietitian + smoking cessation support
expected_management.rationale: Multidisciplinary approach reduces recurrent events by 30-40%
expected_management.mbs_reference: Cardiac rehab program - MBS Group Therapy 81100

expected_management.action: Echocardiogram at 48-72 hours to assess LV function and complications
expected_management.rationale: Quantify LV ejection fraction (likely reduced in anterior STEMI), check for mural thrombus

critical_errors.error: Failure to recognize STEMI on ECG (ST elevation in V1-V4, I, aVL)
critical_errors.consequence: Delayed reperfusion therapy (door-to-balloon >90 min), increased infarct size, mortality risk
critical_errors.correct_action: Immediate STEMI pathway activation, call cardiology/cathlab, aim for PCI within 90 minutes

critical_errors.error: Not administering dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor) immediately
critical_errors.consequence: Increased stent thrombosis risk, higher mortality, larger infarct size
critical_errors.correct_action: Aspirin 300 mg PO (chewed) + Ticagrelor 180 mg PO loading dose ASAP

critical_errors.error: Administering thrombolysis instead of primary PCI when cathlab available <90 min
critical_errors.consequence: Suboptimal reperfusion (thrombolysis 50-60% vs PCI >90% patency), bleeding risk
critical_errors.correct_action: Primary PCI is superior to thrombolysis when available within 90 minutes

critical_errors.error: Delaying analgesia or using NSAIDs (ibuprofen) instead of opioids
critical_errors.consequence: Ongoing sympathetic surge (increases myocardial oxygen demand), NSAIDs increase MI/stroke risk
critical_errors.correct_action: IV morphine 2.5-5 mg for pain relief, avoid NSAIDs absolutely

critical_errors.error: Not monitoring for complications (arrhythmias, heart block, cardiogenic shock)
critical_errors.consequence: Missed VT/VF (reversible if detected early), progression to cardiogenic shock
critical_errors.correct_action: Continuous cardiac monitoring in CCU, frequent vital signs, watch for hypotension/pulmonary oedema

critical_errors.error: Attributing symptoms to 'anxiety' or 'gastritis' due to atypical presentation in female
critical_errors.consequence: Delayed diagnosis (women often have atypical symptoms), increased mortality
critical_errors.correct_action: Low threshold for ECG in all chest pain, especially high-risk patients (diabetes, smoking, FHx)

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACP, Interventional Cardiologist, Royal Melbourne Hospital
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Excellent representation of typical anterior STEMI presentation. Comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension) accurately reflect real-world patient complexity.
fracp_reviews.educational_value: High-yield case for AMC Clinical Exam. Tests time-critical decision-making, ECG interpretation, and knowledge of Australian STEMI pathways.
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: Consider adding troponin delta (repeat at 1 hour) to investigations for completeness.
fracp_reviews.difficulty_calibration: Correctly calibrated as Medium - time-critical management with moderate comorbidity burden, appropriate for AMC standard.

fracp_reviews.reviewer_credentials: FRACP, Director of Coronary Care Unit, Prince of Wales Hospital Sydney
fracp_reviews.clinical_accuracy: Accurate ECG findings and investigation results. Management aligned with NHFA/CSANZ 2023 ACS guidelines.
fracp_reviews.educational_value: Strong case for teaching immediate versus delayed invasive strategy, dual antiplatelet therapy selection, and post-MI risk stratification.
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: Could add mention of radial vs femoral access for PCI (current best practice in Australia is radial-first).
fracp_reviews.difficulty_calibration: Medium difficulty appropriate - sufficient complexity without overwhelming candidates. Good balance of acute management and secondary prevention.

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize STEMI on ECG (ST elevation ≥2 mm in ≥2 contiguous precordial leads or ≥1 mm in limb leads)
Activate time-critical STEMI pathway - door-to-balloon time <90 minutes for primary PCI
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Acute coronary syndrome management, systems-based practice

learning_objectives.objective: Prescribe appropriate dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + ticagrelor/prasugrel) with correct loading doses
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Antiplatelet therapy, PBS restrictions for P2Y12 inhibitors

learning_objectives.objective: Differentiate primary PCI vs thrombolysis based on time to intervention and contraindications
Identify high-risk features in STEMI (anterior location, LV dysfunction, diabetes, age >55)
Implement evidence-based secondary prevention (ACE-I, beta-blocker, high-intensity statin, cardiac rehab)
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Chronic disease management, cardiovascular risk reduction

learning_objectives.objective: Monitor for early complications of anterior MI (VT/VF, heart block, LV failure, mural thrombus)
Apply Australian guidelines (NHFA/CSANZ ACS Guidelines 2023) and understand PBS restrictions for ACS medications
